article.name: Graphicle
article.summary: Graphicle is a local Rust application that combines a code graph, project documents and sessions, reviewed memory, MCP tools, a CLI, and a browser app. Agent-proposed memories remain drafts until approval; retrieval can return source excerpts and reviewed memories with citations. This is a source review, not a runtime evaluation.

contact.note: The official project website publishes info@karlexai.com. The pinned README and SECURITY.md were also checked; neither was used as an email source. No commit/profile metadata or third-party directory was used.

who_what.text: The official README describes Graphicle as a Rust port of Graphify with project memory, delivered as a local program for coding agents. Its components include the graphicle CLI/server, graph and memory crates, an app, and SDKs; the README describes no account or telemetry for local use.
The repository identifies KarLex AI, Inc. as copyright holder, while the project page publishes its contact email. This review does not infer individual maintainer identity from commit metadata.

architecture.text: Graphicle combines a parsed code graph with source documents, reviewed memories, and captured Claude Code/Codex sessions. Its README describes a local application with one data folder, CLI, browser app, and MCP server; the documented default persistence is SQLite.

Memory records are stored per repository with a current row and a revision journal. Structured recall metadata has a named identity, aliases, optional semantic scopes, active/historical/resolved/open-question state, validity interval, and supersession reference. This semantic scope is distinct from authorization to a project or source.

behavior.text: Write: MCP learning tools propose memory drafts with quotes that must match current authorized source text. Drafts are withheld from recall until a person with approval permission reviews them; direct member-reviewed notes follow a separate approve-authorized path.

Update and correction: writes use optimistic revision checks and append revision records. Structured supersession requires an accessible current reviewed target, matching semantic scopes, active states, an expected revision, and an explicit effective time; the old validity interval closes at the replacement's start.

Delete and forgetting: the code documents deletion of source documents, connectors, and projects, removes controlled derived artifacts, checks residue, and creates a hash-chained receipt. Its own contract excludes prior backups, provider retention of requests already sent, and copies exported before deletion; receipts report residue rather than hide it.

Retrieval: memory search supports exact whole-word identity matching against declared names/aliases and a separate explicit lexical discovery mode. Scope, state, and valid-time checks are eligibility filters; lexical mode uses term overlap with inverse document frequency weighting and results are capped by the requested limit. The MCP recall path combines code, documents, sessions, and reviewed memory into cited context within a token budget and does not call a model itself.

Freshness and evidence: cited quotes must occur in an authorized current source; memory records retain source identifiers, hashes, and dependencies. Reads verify repository-file content against SHA-256, and source changes can mark dependent memories stale and withhold them until refreshed and reviewed.

Operational observability: retrieval packets report selected memories/evidence, withheld unreviewed or stale counts, matching mode, temporal parameters, and explicitly state that semantic entailment was not verified. Workflow status exposes queued work and model usage; query logging is opt-in for graph queries. These are code/document interfaces, not measured usefulness.

metrics.evidence: Source code exposes identity and lexical selection and cited context, but no benchmark responses were produced or scored.
Revision checks and effective-time supersession are implemented; no correction sequence or probes were run.
Controlled deletion and receipts are implemented, but no fixture deletion or post-delete probe was run; documented external-copy limits remain.
Project and credential access controls exist, but no cross-project or workspace isolation workload was run.
Exact source-quote validation and source citations are implemented; semantic entailment is explicitly not verified and no responses were adjudicated.
No runtime timing samples were collected.
The project has configurable context budgets and a local store, but no token, cost, or storage measurements were collected for this review.

limits.text: The identity-only or lexical memory selector is not a semantic-entailment judge. The retrieval response explicitly sets semantic_entailment_verified to false; exact quote presence establishes source membership, not that the quote supports every generated interpretation.

A project MCP connection constrains memory and document recall to its project, but its graph tools can address other projects accessible to the credential. Workspace recall searches up to eight accessible projects by default; a normal local MCP connection uses the saved credential, which may be the owner's key and can read all projects. Least-privilege credential setup matters.

Deletion receipts cover the state Graphicle controls; earlier backups, provider-side retention and previously exported copies are outside the stated guarantee. No runtime isolation or deletion probe was run in this review.

benchmark.note: No Graphicle runtime, test suite, or benchmark workload was run. The official README contains upstream-reported figures for particular pre-release versions and configurations; they are not results from this review or this pinned main revision. Project metrics, fixture, and status files define the local evaluation protocol and current not_run state.
